facts.statement: Matrix multiplication is associative $(AB)C = A(BC)$ but generally non-commutative ($AB \ne BA$).
For any square matrix $A$, $A + A^T$ is always symmetric and $A - A^T$ is skew-symmetric.
A square matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if its determinant is non-zero ($|A| \ne 0$, non-singular).
For an $n \times n$ matrix $A$, $|kA| = k^n |A|$ where $k$ is a scalar.
$|\text{adj}(A)| = |A|^{n-1}$ for any square matrix $A$ of order $n$.

definitions.definition: A square matrix whose determinant is strictly non-zero ($|A| \ne 0$).
The transpose of the cofactor matrix of a square matrix $A$.

common_misconceptions.misconception: If AB = 0, then either A = 0 or B = 0.
common_misconceptions.truth: Two non-zero matrices can multiply to yield the zero matrix (zero divisors exist in matrix algebra).
common_misconceptions.why: Row-by-column dot products can sum to zero without components being zero.
